Knowing absolutely nothing about you besides what you posted here, I'd guess that your form is shitty. If your strides are too long, you'll heel strike ahead of your hips. That actually causes you to slow down a couple ways:

1) Your foot strike ahead of your hips creates a backwards force. The force of you landing on your leading foot sends a reaction force straight back up your leg and if it's in front of you instead of directly beneath you, there's a small component in the backwards direction.

2) foot strike ahead of your hips tends to create more vertical motion. Because it's in front of your hips, it's not as 'tall' as your other leg and so your body drops a bit. But as it moves underneath you, your body moves up too. This is not only wasted motion, it puts pressure on your diaphragm every stride and makes it hard to get into a breathing rhythm. Ideally, you should inhale for 2-3 strides then exhale for 2 strides.

Next time you go out, try starting with smaller, quicker steps.
